title: Queue every eligible dependency as its own persistent bead
description:
Inspect fresh origin/main in an isolated clone of
git@github.com:benschac/digitial-garden.git. Confirm the origin and read repository
instructions and packageManager. Do not upgrade Bun or Node or change any source.
Inventory all direct dependencies and devDependencies across the root and
workspaces once. Query registry versions, then choose the newest stable compatible
candidate for each package. Exact pins need an explicit target version.

Stable >=1.0.0 candidates must remain in the current major. Stable 0.x candidates
must remain in the current minor. Check every existing declaration of that package.
Do not downgrade, widen ranges, or update peers, optional dependencies, overrides,
workspace/catalog/file/link/Git/URL/tag/alias dependencies, or ambiguous ranges.
Known breaking changes, engine mismatches, coupled peer upgrades, prereleases,
and packages in scripts/agent-sources.json require review. Prefer an eligible
compatible candidate over a newer breaking release. If only an ineligible newer
release exists, create or reuse its review bead without routing it to a worker.
Never stop inventory after finding the first candidate.

Use persistent task beads in the personal-site rig, never ephemeral beads.
Each candidate has metadata dependency_package, dependency_target, and
dependency_phase (prepare, ready, review, or landed). Its description records
all manifest paths and old declaration values, exact target, inventory base SHA,
registry evidence, and any known release or compatibility caveats.

Before creating work, list ALL states and all rows for the package:

```sh
gc --city "$GC_CITY" --rig personal-site bd list --all --limit 0 --metadata-field dependency_package=PACKAGE --json
```

Replace PACKAGE with the actual package name.
Read existing candidates, including completed ones, and match the exact target.
Also inspect existing dependency-review tasks without this metadata. Reuse a
verified exact package/target match instead of duplicating a legacy review task.
Do not reroute in-progress work, ready publisher work, blocked review work, or
completed work. Reuse an exact-target review or failure without automatically
retrying it. Allow at most one active prepare or ready candidate per package.
A held review for a different target must not block a compatible candidate.
For example, a review of foo@3 must not prevent preparing foo@2.1. Preserve the
held review. Never turn an exact-target failed check into a fresh daily retry.

Create missing candidates using a JSON metadata file and description file:

```sh
gc --city "$GC_CITY" --rig personal-site bd create "$TITLE" --type task --labels dependency-update --metadata @candidate.json --body-file body.md --json
```

Use the returned ID. For compatible candidates, set dependency_phase=prepare
and route the returned bead with this command:

```sh
gc --city "$GC_CITY" sling personal-site/deps.worker "$BEAD" --no-formula --no-convoy
```

Package beads are plain work, not formula wrappers.
For review candidates, set dependency_phase=review, status blocked, and the
dependency-review label. Do not route them to an automatic worker.
If create succeeded but routing did not, reuse and route that same unassigned
prepare bead on restart. Never create another bead merely because dispatch failed.

Record every created, reused, held, and dispatched bead on the scan bead.
Close the scan bead after inventory and routing, without waiting for package
workers. Drain the scanner session. The singleton scanner and scheduler overlap
gate avoid routine concurrent inventory; do not manually launch a second scanner.

Stable >=1.0.0 candidates must remain in the current major. Stable 0.x candidates
must remain in the current minor. Check every existing declaration of that package.
Do not downgrade, widen ranges, or update peers, optional dependencies, overrides,
workspace/catalog/file/link/Git/URL/tag/alias dependencies, or ambiguous ranges.
Known breaking changes, engine mismatches, coupled peer upgrades, prereleases,
and packages in scripts/agent-sources.json require review. Prefer an eligible
compatible candidate over a newer breaking release. If only an ineligible newer
release exists, create or reuse its review bead without routing it to a worker.
Never stop inventory after finding the first candidate.

Use persistent task beads in the personal-site rig, never ephemeral beads.
Each candidate has metadata dependency_package, dependency_target, and
dependency_phase (prepare, ready, review, or landed). Its description records
all manifest paths and old declaration values, exact target, inventory base SHA,
registry evidence, and any known release or compatibility caveats.

Before creating work, list ALL states and all rows for the package:

```sh
gc --city "$GC_CITY" --rig personal-site bd list --all --limit 0 --metadata-field dependency_package=PACKAGE --json
```

Replace PACKAGE with the actual package name.
Read existing candidates, including completed ones, and match the exact target.
Also inspect existing dependency-review tasks without this metadata. Reuse a
verified exact package/target match instead of duplicating a legacy review task.
Do not reroute in-progress work, ready publisher work, blocked review work, or
completed work. Reuse an exact-target review or failure without automatically
retrying it. Allow at most one active prepare or ready candidate per package.
A held review for a different target must not block a compatible candidate.
For example, a review of foo@3 must not prevent preparing foo@2.1. Preserve the
held review. Never turn an exact-target failed check into a fresh daily retry.

Create missing candidates using a JSON metadata file and description file:

```sh
gc --city "$GC_CITY" --rig personal-site bd create "$TITLE" --type task --labels dependency-update --metadata @candidate.json --body-file body.md --json
```

Use the returned ID. For compatible candidates, set dependency_phase=prepare
and route the returned bead with this command:

```sh
gc --city "$GC_CITY" sling personal-site/deps.worker "$BEAD" --no-formula --no-convoy
```

Package beads are plain work, not formula wrappers.
For review candidates, set dependency_phase=review, status blocked, and the
dependency-review label. Do not route them to an automatic worker.
If create succeeded but routing did not, reuse and route that same unassigned
prepare bead on restart. Never create another bead merely because dispatch failed.

Record every created, reused, held, and dispatched bead on the scan bead.

workers. Drain the scanner session. The singleton scanner and scheduler overlap
gate avoid routine concurrent inventory; do not manually launch a second scanner.

title: Publish one compatible dependency or record why no update is eligible
description:
Work only in a new temporary clone of git@github.com:benschac/digitial-garden.git.
Fetch origin/main, create the working branch from that exact commit, and record
the base SHA. Confirm the clone is clean and origin is the expected repository.
Read its AGENTS.md instructions and packageManager pin. Use that Bun version.
Do not upgrade Bun or Node as part of this order.

Inspect direct dependencies and devDependencies in the root and workspaces.
Query the registry for available versions. Check official release notes for the
candidate range. Exact pins require an explicitly selected target version.
Do not use an unqualified bun update, wildcards, or --latest.

Eligible updates have stable current and target versions. For versions >=1.0.0,
the target must stay within the current major. For 0.x, the target must stay
within the current minor. A semver-compatible number is not proof of safety:
hold documented breaking changes, uncertain compatibility, engine mismatches,
and peer changes requiring another direct package for review. Do not downgrade.
Skip workspace, catalog, file, link, Git, URL, tag, alias, and ambiguous ranges.
Hold every package named in scripts/agent-sources.json for source-reference review.
Do not update dependency overrides, peerDependencies, or optionalDependencies.

Choose one eligible package. Consider the rest when an earlier candidate is
ineligible so a held package cannot starve later packages. For each held upgrade,
find or create one persistent review task keyed by package and target version,
labelled dependency-review. Record the current and target versions, release-note
links, and the reason. Reuse an existing matching task rather than creating daily
duplicates. Never route these review tasks back to the updater automatically.
If no candidate is eligible, record that outcome and finish without a commit.

For the selected package, update its existing dependency or devDependency
declarations to the chosen version using the pinned Bun CLI's explicit package
version update operation. Preserve exact pins and existing range operators.
Do not add a declaration where the package was not already declared. If Bun
cannot express this narrowly, edit only those existing version values and run
the pinned Bun install to regenerate the root bun.lock. Never edit lock entries
by hand. Keep all declarations of this one package consistent where compatible.

Inspect the complete diff. Only this package's existing declaration values and
the root bun.lock may change. Transitive lock changes must belong to the selected
package's necessary dependency closure. Reject unrelated resolution churn,
new lockfiles, trust changes, source changes, and companion package updates.
Do not fix unrelated failures or relax checks to make this update pass.

Run bun install --frozen-lockfile, git diff --check, and focused checks appropriate
to the changed dependency. Run TURBO_SCM_BASE=HEAD TURBO_SCM_HEAD=HEAD bun run verify
before committing. Check command exit statuses and inspect their results.
Do not run a local production build or verify:full for this order. The operator
accepts Vercel build validation after publication. A failed check means no push.
Record a review task with the failure and preserve evidence for a later attempt.

Stage only the inspected manifest paths and root bun.lock. Inspect the staged
diff and run git diff --cached --check. Commit exactly once with a message such
as chore(deps): update package from old to new. Confirm HEAD has exactly one
commit beyond the recorded base and contains only the approved files.

Fetch origin/main again immediately before publication. If it differs from the
recorded base, stop this attempt without rebasing or pushing. Record the race
and let a later invocation start again from fresh main. Otherwise run a normal
git push origin HEAD:main. Never use --force or --force-with-lease. If the server
rejects the push, stop and record the rejection without changing branch rules.
After pushing, fetch origin/main and verify the new commit is in its history.
If the push response is uncertain, inspect that history before any retry.

Append a result to the claimed bead with the package, old and new versions,
release-note evidence, base SHA, commit SHA if created, checks and exit statuses,
push result, and any review-task IDs. Distinguish local verification from a
Vercel deployment result. Do not claim a successful build without observing it.
Close the claimed work bead and run gc runtime drain-ack. Keep review tasks
separate from the completed scheduled run. Remove only a clone created by this
invocation after success or a no-op. Preserve an unpushed commit or failed-check
clone and record its path when it is needed for review.
